claims.text: The proposed material is an Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti high-entropy alloy.
Increasing the aluminum content of the Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti alloy will reduce its density.
Optimized processing can control the evolution and distribution of secondary precipitates in the alloy matrix.
Controlled secondary precipitates will reinforce the alloy matrix.
Controlled precipitate formation will compensate for potential strength losses caused by compositional modification.
Increasing aluminum content while controlling precipitate evolution will preserve or enhance the alloy's mechanical properties.
The proposed compositional and processing changes will reduce density by approximately 10-20%.
The modified alloy will maintain or improve tensile strength relative to conventional designs.
The modified alloy will maintain or improve ductility relative to conventional designs.
The modified alloy will maintain or improve fatigue resistance relative to conventional designs.
The conventional initial alloy has relatively high density because it contains lower proportions of lightweight elements.
Conventional high-entropy alloys or lightweight composites typically exhibit a trade-off between reduced weight and comprehensive performance.
The optimized performance may be limited to typical structural loading temperatures and stresses.
Extreme operating conditions could produce performance different from the predicted outcome.
Failure to achieve at least a 10% density reduction while also failing to maintain or improve mechanical properties is designated as a falsifying result.
